sentences.text: A 2001 study analyzed 115 gastroliths found associated with a Cedarosaurus specimen, with a total mass of 7 kilograms.

Fossils of Cedarosaurus were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, while other fossils come from the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Formation in western Utah and the Paluxy Formation in Texas, USA.
Cedarosaurus was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter, and Brooks in 1999.
Researchers suggest the high surface area of the largest gastroliths indicates they may have helped grind or crush ingested plant material.
Cedarosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
The type species of the genus Cedarosaurus is Cedarosaurus weiskopfae.
